newsitem.title: UK: Doughty Hanson buys Swiss Geberit.
newsitem.headline: Doughty Hanson buys Swiss Geberit.

text.p: Private fund manager Doughty Hanson & Co said on Tuesday it had acquired Swiss sanitary system company Geberit for 1.8 billion Swiss francs ($1.2 billion).
Doughty Hanson said in a statement the business would continue to be run by the existing management team, who will become shareholders under the transaction. ($ = 1.480 Swiss Francs)

Family-owned Geberit International AG, a leading producer of sanitary systems in Europe with strong market share particularly in Germany, Switzerland, Austria and Italy, is based in Rapperswil, Switzerland. Last year it said it was reviewing its future, including a possible flotation.
Doughty Hanson and Geberit said on Tuesday they aimed to achieve an initial public offering of shares in Geberit within the next three to five years.
Geberit estimated its 1996 earnings before interest and tax at 138.8 million Swiss francs on turnover of 905 million.

"With our new partner we will continue to pursue our strategic objectives to develop our leading sanitary expertise and to increase the internationalisation of the business, where appropriate through acquisitions and joint ventures," Geberit chairman Guenter Kelm said, welcoming the move.

Doughty Hanson & Co, with offices in London, Frankfurt and Stockholm, manages the largest independent private equity fund in Europe and has achieved stock market listings for companies with an aggregate value of more than 2.9 billion marks since 1995.
